artboards.title: Option A — Two tabs, one job each
Option B — One scroll, no tabs
Option C — Viewer first, peek sheet

annotations.text:
YASTL model detail panel

Measured on the live instance at 390px (Pixel 7). The panel carries 58 interactive controls across a header, a 10-control toolbar, 3 tabs and an action row. More holds 8 equal-weight sections and 1358px of scroll.

Three directions below differ on one axis: how much structure survives. A keeps tabs, B removes them, C makes the viewer the page.

The two things you see first in More are a Telegram advert from someone else's download and a 12-tile grid that is a listing of every image in the parent folder — hence the sloth and the stranger's selfie.

Related Models below it is 50 siblings in alphabetical order.

Smallest change that fixes the ranked problems. Overview answers 'will this print', Organise holds tags/collections/print log. Everything that was a section becomes a row with a count, so nothing loads or renders until asked for.

Cheapest to build. Keeps the tab pattern people already know.

No tabs at all — one scroll of collapsed groups in task order, with the viewer pinned as a shrinking header so you can read and look at once.

Best for a long tail of rarely-used sections. Costs a scroll-linked header, which is the fiddliest part on iOS Safari.

The viewer IS the screen; a peek sheet carries dimensions, the bed verdict and the one action, and drags up for everything else.

Best triage experience and the only one that makes the 3D view feel like the point. Most work, and the drag sheet has to be built properly.
The toolbar decision is separable — it applies to whichever direction you pick.
